steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.

title: Compression Does Not End at Selection: Post-Selection Positional Geometry for Sparse KV Caches
summary: RoPERelay replaces the default practice of retaining original full-history RoPE coordinates in a sparse KV cache; after selection, it compacts coordinates in an order-preserving way by inverse-rotating and re-rotating cached key phases and synchronizing the current query, without renewed selection, re-prefill, or extra cache budget. It costs roughly 1%-3% additional request latency in the evaluated configurations plus implementation complexity in the inference path, with no extra memory or cache footprint. It can fail if the serving stack does not expose per-key positional manipulation, if the model uses non-RoPE positional schemes, or if gains do not transfer beyond the evaluated long-term memory tasks and selectors to the reader's workloads.
rationale: The method is inexpensive and compatible with existing selectors and caches, but its quality gains are demonstrated on a narrow set of long-memory tasks and models, so workload-specific validation is warranted before production adoption.

claims.statement: RoPERelay replaces the default practice of retaining original full-history RoPE coordinates in a sparse KV cache; after selection, it compacts coordinates in an order-preserving way by inverse-rotating and re-rotating cached key phases and synchronizing the current query, without renewed selection, re-prefill, or extra cache budget. It costs roughly 1%-3% additional request latency in the evaluated configurations plus implementation complexity in the inference path, with no extra memory or cache footprint. It can fail if the serving stack does not expose per-key positional manipulation, if the model uses non-RoPE positional schemes, or if gains do not transfer beyond the evaluated long-term memory tasks and selectors to the reader's workloads.

Improves answer quality in 32 of 36 comparisons across two models, six sparse selectors, and three long-term memory tasks; e.g., Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct with BM25 on LongMemEval-S rises from 23.6% to 35.4% accuracy, with approximately 1%-3% complete-request time overhead.
